Selected Work

Financial Statement Analysis & Visualization

Tableau · Financial Statement Analysis · Data Visualization · Storytelling

Two interactive Tableau dashboards that turn the ABC Company’s multi-year balance sheet and income statement data into a clearer view of financial position, operating performance, and change over time.

Prepared by Alexander Jenkins

Project Overview

I used Tableau to build two financial dashboards that organize and visualize the ABC Company’s balance sheet and income statement data across multiple years. The project combines financial statement analysis with interactive data visualization to make trends in profitability, liquidity, efficiency, working capital, and financial risk easier to evaluate.

Rather than presenting financial data only through traditional statements and tables, I structured the dashboards to help tell the story behind the numbers by highlighting key financial measures, relationships, and changes over time.

Tools & Methods

  • Financial Statement Analysis
  • Ratio Analysis
  • Trend Analysis

View Balance Sheet Dashboard ↗

The Objective

Financial statements contain a significant amount of information by nature, but evaluating performance requires understanding how individual accounts and financial ratios relate to one another over time.

The objective of this project was to use Tableau to organize financial information into dashboards that make those relationships easier to identify. The broader goal was to demonstrate how financial data can be transformed into a visual story that helps management understand what is changing within a company or helps investors evaluate its financial performance and position.

Balance Sheet & Financial Position

The balance sheet dashboard organizes assets, liabilities, and owners’ equity while incorporating financial measures related to liquidity, working capital, operating efficiency, and risk.

The dashboard includes measures such as the current ratio, quick ratio, asset turnover, return on capital employed, gearing, interest coverage, and other working-capital indicators. Presenting these measures alongside the balance sheet provides additional context for evaluating changes in the company’s financial position across the period analyzed.

Gearing was a term that was new to me when completing this project. Researching the concept helped me better understand how leverage measures can be constructed and interpreted differently depending on the context. In this dashboard, the gearing measure uses cumulative liabilities relative to cumulative assets across the periods displayed, allowing the dashboard to show how the relationship between the two measures developed over time.

This portion of the project allowed me to connect financial statement accounts with the ratios commonly used to evaluate liquidity, efficiency, leverage, and financial risk.

Profitability & Operating Performance

The second dashboard focuses on the company’s income statement and operating performance. It presents sales, gross profit, EBITDA, operating profit, PBIT, and net profit while also visualizing changes in revenue, margins, and profitability over time.

View Income Statement Dashboard ↗

Combining the financial tables with trend and comparison charts made it possible to examine both the reported results and the direction of the company’s performance within the same dashboard.

What I Built

I developed two Tableau dashboards using financial statement data from the ABC Company. The dashboards combine detailed accounting information with calculated financial measures and visualizations designed to make multi-year financial performance easier to interpret.

The project required organizing financial data into appropriate categories, selecting financial measures relevant to each statement, creating calculated metrics and ratios, and determining how those measures could be presented together within a usable dashboard.
